words.ex: The boy has an abnormal heartbeat.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的心跳不正常。
words.en: Deviating from what is normal or usual, typically in a way that is undesirable or worrying.

words.ex: The passengers are aboard the plane.
words.ex_cn: 乘客们在飞机上。
words.en: On or onto a ship, aircraft, bus, or train.

words.ex: She decided to have an abortion.
words.ex_cn: 她决定进行流产。
words.en: An abortion is a medical procedure to end a pregnancy so it does not result in the birth of a baby.

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.ex: The teacher said the answer is acceptable.
words.ex_cn: 老师说这个答案是可以接受的。
words.en: Something that is acceptable is satisfactory or good enough to be allowed or approved of.

words.ex: His acceptance of the offer made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了这份提议，让大家都很高兴。
words.en: The act of agreeing to receive or undertake something offered.

words.tr: v. 接受；“accept”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 公认的；
words.ex: He accepted the gift with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着接受了这份礼物。
words.en: Generally agreed to be correct or satisfactory.

words.ex: He bought a new accessory for his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的手机买了一个新配件。
words.en: An accessory is something such as a bag or piece of jewelry that you wear or carry because it is attractive.

words.tr: adj. 受欢呼的；受赞誉的； v. “acclaim”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The acclaimed actor received a standing ovation.
words.ex_cn: 这位受欢呼的演员赢得了起立鼓掌。
words.en: Publicly praised; celebrated.

words.ex: He worked hard to accomplish his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的目标。
words.en: To accomplish something means to succeed in doing it, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: He faced an accusation of stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他面临偷钱的指控。
words.en: An accusation is a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: I met him at a party, but he is only an acquaintance.
words.ex_cn: 我在聚会上认识了他，但他只是个熟人。
words.en: An acquaintance is someone you know a little, who is not a close friend.

words.ex: The adaptation of animals to cold weather is amazing.
words.ex_cn: 动物对寒冷天气的适应令人惊叹。
words.en: An adaptation is a film, television drama, or stage play that is based on a written work.

words.ex: The game is addictive and hard to stop playing.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏令人上瘾，很难停止玩。
words.en: If a substance or activity is addictive, it makes you want more of it so that you become dependent on it.

words.ex: The administration of the school is very organized.
words.ex_cn: 学校的行政管理非常有条理。
words.en: The process or activity of running a business, organization, etc., or the people who run it.

words.ex: The administrative office handles school records.
words.ex_cn: 行政办公室负责管理学校档案。
words.en: Relating to the management of a company, organization, or institution.

words.ex: The administrator fixed the computer system.
words.ex_cn: 管理人员修复了计算机系统。
words.en: An administrator is a person whose job involves helping to organize and supervise the way that an organization or institution functions.

words.ex: He is an adviser to the government.
words.ex_cn: 他是政府的顾问。
words.en: An adviser is a person who gives advice, especially someone who knows a lot about a particular subject.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: This phone is affordable for students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机对学生来说价格合理。
words.en: If something is affordable, most people have enough money to buy it.

words.ex: The agency helps people find jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这个机构帮助人们找工作。
words.en: An agency is a business which provides a service on behalf of other businesses.

words.ex: We will review the meeting agenda tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将审查会议议程。
words.en: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done or considered, especially in a meeting.

words.ex: The aggression of the army caused many deaths.
words.ex_cn: 军队的侵略导致了许多人死亡。
words.en: Aggression is a violent or hostile behavior towards another person or country.

words.tr:
n. 帮助；援助；
v. 帮助；协助；
words.ex: The charity provided aid to the flood victims.
words.ex_cn: 慈善机构向洪水受害者提供了帮助。
words.en: To aid someone means to help or assist them. Aid can also refer to the help or support given.

words.tr:
n. 警报；闹钟；惊慌；
v. 使惊恐；
words.ex: The fire alarm rang loudly.
words.ex_cn: 火警警报大声响了起来。
words.en: An alarm is a warning of danger, often given by a bell or flashing light.

words.tr: adj. 使人惊恐的；引起恐慌的； v. “alarm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The news report showed an alarming rise in crimes.
words.ex_cn: 新闻报道显示犯罪率令人惊恐地上升。
words.en: If something is alarming, it makes you feel afraid or anxious that something unpleasant or dangerous might happen.

words.tr:
adj. 警觉的；警惕的；
n. 警报；
v. （使）警惕；（使）戒备；
words.ex: The alert guard noticed the strange movement.
words.ex_cn: 这位警觉的警卫注意到了奇怪的动静。
words.en: If you are alert, you are paying full attention to things around you and are able to deal with anything that might happen.

words.ex: He denied the allegation of stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了偷钱的指控。
words.en: An allegation is a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal.

words.tr: v. 声称；“allege”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 所谓的；
words.ex: He alleged that the witness lied.
words.ex_cn: 他声称证人说了谎。
words.en: An alleged fact has been stated but has not been proved.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 允许；留出；给予；承认；
words.ex: My parents allow me to go out on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 我的父母允许我周末外出。
words.en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.ex: France was an ally of the United States in the war.
words.ex_cn: 法国在战争中是美国的同盟者。
words.en: An ally is a country, organization, or person that helps and supports another country, organization, or person in a difficult situation.

words.ex: He walked alongside the river.
words.ex_cn: 他沿着河边走。
words.en: If one thing is alongside another thing, the first thing is next to the second.

words.ex: The alteration of the dress made it fit better.
words.ex_cn: 这件衣服的修改让它更合身了。
words.en: An alteration is a change in or to something.

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr:
n. 业余爱好者；
adj. 业余的；
words.ex: He is an amateur who paints on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他是个周末画画的业余爱好者。
words.en: An amateur is someone who does something as a hobby and not as a job.

words.ex: The amendment changed the old law.
words.ex_cn: 这项修正案改变了旧法律。
words.en: An amendment is a change or addition to a law or document.

words.ex: He stood amid the trees, quiet and still.
words.ex_cn: 他站在树木中间，安静而静止。
words.en: If something is amid other things, it is surrounded by them.

words.ex: There is ample food for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有足够的食物。
words.en: If there is an ample amount of something, there is enough of it and usually some extra.

words.tr: adj. 分析的；善于分析的；
words.ex: He uses analytical skills to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用分析能力解决数学问题。
words.en: An analytical way of doing something involves the use of logical reasoning.

words.ex: The angle of the roof helps rain run off.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶的角度有助于雨水流下。
words.en: An angle is the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, measured in degrees.

words.ex: The loud noise was an annoyance to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 那阵噪音让每个人都感到烦恼。
words.en: Annoyance is the feeling of being slightly angry or impatient.

words.tr: adj. 反社会的；危害社会的；厌恶社交的；不合群的
words.ex: He is antisocial and rarely talks to others.
words.ex_cn: 他性格孤僻，很少与别人交谈。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as antisocial, you mean that it shows an unwillingness to associate with or be friendly with other people.

words.ex: I anticipate rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我预料明天会下雨。
words.en: If you anticipate an event, you realize in advance that it may happen and you are prepared for it.

words.tr: adj. 骇人的； v. “appall”的现在分词；
words.ex: The accident caused an appalling sight.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了一幅骇人的景象。
words.en: If you describe something as appalling, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or unpleasant, and that you find it extremely unacceptable.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.ex: The crowd applauded after the performance.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: To applaud means to show approval or praise by clapping the hands.

words.ex: The audience gave applause after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌曲结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: Applause is the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands to show approval or enjoyment.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.ex: The boss appointed Tom as the new manager.
words.ex_cn: 老板任命汤姆为新经理。
words.en: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

words.ex: The archaeologist found an old pot in the ground.
words.ex_cn: 这位考古学家在地下发现了一个旧陶罐。
words.en: An archaeologist is someone who studies the societies and cultures of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: He loves archaeology and digs old artifacts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱考古学，挖掘古代文物。
words.en: Archaeology is the study of the societies and peoples of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: A problem arose during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议中出现了一个问题。
words.en: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

words.ex: The arrival of the train was delayed by 20 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 火车的到达晚了20分钟。
words.en: The act of coming to a place or the moment when something or someone arrives.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.ex: The teacher will assign homework today.
words.ex_cn: 老师今天会布置作业。
words.en: To give someone a particular job or task; to allocate a resource or responsibility to a particular person or purpose.

words.ex: The teacher gave us a math assignment.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我们布置了一份数学作业。
words.en: An assignment is a task or piece of work that you are given to do, especially as part of your job or studies.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: He gave me his assurance that the work would be done on time.
words.ex_cn: 他向我保证工作会按时完成。
words.en: If you give someone an assurance that something is true or will happen, you say that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, in order to make them feel less worried.

words.tr:
n. 攻击；袭击；
v. 攻击；袭击；
words.ex: The attack happened at night.
words.ex_cn: 这次攻击发生在夜晚。
words.en: To attack means to try to hurt or defeat someone or something by using force or violence.

words.ex: He worked hard to attain his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以达到他的目标。
words.en: If you attain something, you gain it or achieve it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: His attendance at the meeting was mandatory.
words.ex_cn: 他必须出席这次会议。
words.en: The act of being present at a place or event.

words.ex: The old painting was sold at an auction.
words.ex_cn: 那幅旧画在拍卖会上被卖出了。
words.en: An auction is a public sale where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder.

words.tr:
n. 试听；试唱；试演；听力
v. 试听；试音；试镜；让…试演
words.ex: He went to an audition for the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他去参加学校话剧的试听。
words.en: An audition is a short performance given by an actor, dancer, or musician so that someone can decide if they are good enough to be in a play, film, or orchestra.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.ex: There are many shops on this avenue.
words.ex_cn: 这条大街上有许多商店。
words.en: An avenue is a wide street or main thoroughfare, often lined with trees or other landscaping.

words.ex: He has awareness of the environmental problems.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到环境问题。
words.en: Knowledge or perception of a situation or fact.

words.ex: Bacteria can make you sick.
words.ex_cn: 细菌会让你生病。
words.en: Bacteria are very small organisms. Some bacteria can cause diseases.

words.ex: The company is bankrupt after losing all its money.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司失去所有钱后破产了。
words.en: If a person or a company is bankrupt, they have been declared by a court of law to be unable to pay their debts.

words.ex: The bird uses its beak to eat seeds.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟用它的喙吃种子。
words.en: The hard, pointed, often curved part of a bird's mouth, used for picking up and eating food.

words.tr:
v. 敢说；
n. 打赌；赌注；
words.ex: I bet you didn't know that.
words.ex_cn: 我敢说你不知道那件事。
words.en: If you bet on the result of a horse race, football game, or other event, you give someone a sum of money which they give you back with extra money if the result is what you predicted, or which they keep if it is not.

words.ex: Beware of the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当心那只狗。
words.en: to be cautious and alert to the dangers of.

words.tr: adj. 有偏见的； v. “bias”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The judge was biased against the defendant.
words.ex_cn: 这位法官对被告有偏见。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.tr:
n. 努力争取；出价；投标；
v. 出价；投标；
words.ex: His bid for the championship inspired everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他为冠军所做的努力鼓舞了所有人。
words.en: To bid means to offer a particular amount of money for something that is being sold, especially at an auction, or to offer to do work or provide services for a particular price.

words.tr: adj. 两种语言的；用两种语言的；
words.ex: He is a bilingual student who speaks English and Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个会说英语和西班牙语的双语学生。
words.en: A bilingual person is someone who can speak two languages equally well.

words.ex: His birth was in a small village.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在一个小村庄。
words.en: The emergence of a baby or other young from the body of its mother; the start of life as a physically separate being.

words.ex: His blindness made him rely on his hearing.
words.ex_cn: 他的失明让他依赖听觉。
words.en: Blindness is the condition of being unable to see because of injury, disease, or a congenital condition.

words.tr: adj. 一定会；密切相关的；有义务的； v. “bind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is bound to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会赢得比赛。
words.en: If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other. If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.

words.ex: The fence marks the boundary between the two gardens.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏标志着两个花园的分界线。
words.en: A boundary is a real or imagined line that marks the edge or limit of something.

words.ex: He bought a brass lamp at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个黄铜制品台灯。
words.en: Brass is a yellow-coloured metal made from copper and zinc. It is used especially for making ornaments and musical instruments.

words.ex: He tried to bribe the officer with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱贿赂官员。
words.en: A bribe is a sum of money or something valuable that one person offers or gives to another in order to persuade them to do something, usually something dishonest.

words.ex: Reading books can broaden your mind.
words.ex_cn: 读书可以扩大你的视野。
words.en: If something broadens or if you broaden it, it increases in size or range.

words.ex: The rule applies broadly across all schools.
words.ex_cn: 这个规定广泛适用于所有学校。
words.en: In a general way; without considering details.

words.ex: The statue is made of bronze.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像由青铜制成。
words.en: Bronze is a yellowish-brown metal which is a mixture of copper and tin.

words.ex: The storm caused a brutal flood that destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了残酷的洪水，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.

words.ex: The child blew a bubble with gum.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用口香糖吹了一个气泡。
words.en: A bubble is a small ball of air or gas in a liquid, or a ball of air inside a solid substance such as glass.

words.tr: adj. 庞大的；肥大的；体积大的；
words.ex: The box is too bulky to fit in the car.
words.ex_cn: 这个箱子太大了，放不进车里。
words.en: Something that is bulky is large and heavy, and therefore difficult to move or carry.

words.ex: He bullies his little brother every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都欺负他的弟弟。
words.en: To bully someone means to use your strength or power to hurt or frighten them, often forcing them to do something they do not want to do.

words.ex: The heavy workload became a burden for her.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量成了她的负担。
words.en: A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry, or a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear.

words.ex: The sailors slept in the cabin during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 水手们在风暴期间睡在船舱里。
words.en: A cabin is a small room or compartment, especially one on a ship or an aircraft.

words.tr: n. （政治、商业或社会性）活动；运动；
words.ex: The city launched a campaign to reduce plastic waste.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市发起了一项减少塑料垃圾的活动。
words.en: A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change.

words.tr: n. 取消；撤销；作废；中止；
words.ex: The flight cancellation made us wait for a new ticket.
words.ex_cn: 航班取消让我们不得不等待新的机票。
words.en: The act of cancelling something; a situation in which something that has been arranged is stopped from happening.

words.ex: He showed great capability in solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决数学问题上展现了很强的能力。
words.en: The ability or qualities necessary to do something.

words.ex: The king rode in a wooden carriage drawn by four horses.
words.ex_cn: 国王乘坐一辆由四匹马拉的木制四轮马车。
words.en: A carriage is a vehicle with four wheels that is pulled by horses and is used for carrying people.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.tr:
n. 小心；警告；注意；
v. 警告；劝...小心；
words.ex: He drove with caution on the icy road.
words.ex_cn: 他在结冰的道路上小心驾驶。
words.en: Caution is care that you take in order to avoid possible danger or trouble.

words.ex: The central park is in the middle of the city.
words.ex_cn: 中央公园位于城市中心。
words.en: Something that is central is of key or fundamental importance.

words.ex: The weather is changeable in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天的天气是多变的。
words.en: If something is changeable, it can be changed or it changes often.

words.ex: The room was chaotic after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后房间一片混乱。
words.en: If a situation, place, or system is chaotic, it is in a state of complete disorder and confusion.

words.tr: adj. 爱说话的；爱讲闲话的；饶舌的
words.ex: She is chatty during lunch break.
words.ex_cn: 她在午餐休息时很健谈。
words.en: If you describe someone as chatty, you mean that they enjoy talking in a friendly, informal way.

words.tr: adj. 寒冷的；冷淡的；冷漠的；
words.ex: The morning air was chilly.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的空气很寒冷。
words.en: Something that is chilly is unpleasantly cold.

words.ex: He eats eggs but watches his cholesterol.
words.ex_cn: 他吃鸡蛋，但注意自己的胆固醇。
words.en: Cholesterol is a substance that exists in the cells of the body and in blood, which can cause heart disease if there is too much of it.

words.tr: n. 令人讨厌的或繁重的工作；
words.ex: Washing dishes is a boring chore.
words.ex_cn: 洗碗是一件烦人的琐事。
words.en: A chore is a task or piece of work that is often boring or unpleasant but needs to be done regularly.

words.tr: adj. 国内的；公民的；民用的；
words.ex: The country is recovering from a civil war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在从一场内战中恢复。
words.en: relating to ordinary citizens and their concerns, as distinct from military or ecclesiastical matters.

words.ex: He asked for clarification about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他要求对规则进行澄清。
words.en: A clarification is a statement that makes something clear or easier to understand.

words.ex: Can you clarify your answer?
words.ex_cn: 你能澄清一下你的答案吗？
words.en: To clarify something means to make it easier to understand by explaining it more clearly.

words.ex: The teacher will classify the students by age.
words.ex_cn: 老师将按年龄对学生进行分类。
words.en: To classify things means to divide them into groups or types so that things with similar characteristics are in the same group.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a clinical exam.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他做了临床检查。
words.en: Clinical means involving or relating to the direct observation and treatment of patients, rather than theoretical or laboratory studies.

words.tr: n. 亲密；接近；密闭；狭窄
words.ex: The closeness of the two friends is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 这两位朋友之间的亲密显而易见。
words.en: The state of being close in space or time; intimacy or familiarity.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；攫住
n. 紧抓；离合器；一窝雏；一小群；紧要关头
words.ex: He clutched the rope tightly when he slipped.
words.ex_cn: 当他滑倒时，他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To clutch something means to hold it tightly, usually because you are afraid or anxious. In a vehicle, the clutch is a pedal that you press with your foot to change gears.

words.ex: He burns coal to keep his house warm.
words.ex_cn: 他烧煤来让房子暖和。
words.en: Coal is a hard black substance that is extracted from the ground and burned as fuel.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.ex: The two companies worked together in collaboration.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司通过合作一起工作。
words.en: the act of working together with someone to produce or create something

words.ex: Wheat is a basic commodity in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 小麦在许多国家是一种基本商品。
words.en: A commodity is something that is bought and sold.

words.tr: adj. 常见的；普通的；共有的；
words.ex: Colds are a common illness in winter.
words.ex_cn: 感冒在冬天是很常见的疾病。
words.en: Something that is common happens often or is found in many places.

words.ex: He commonly eats breakfast at 7 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他一般在早上七点吃早餐。
words.en: If something is commonly the case, it is usually or often the case.

words.tr:
n. 通勤；
v. 通勤；
words.ex: His daily commute takes an hour by train.
words.ex_cn: 他每天的通勤坐火车要一个小时。
words.en: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

words.tr: adj. 可比较的；比得上的；类似的；
words.ex: The prices of these two phones are comparable.
words.ex_cn: 这两部手机的价格是可比较的。
words.en: Something that is comparable to something else is similar in size, amount, or quality.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.ex: The company will compensate you for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 公司会因延误而补偿你。
words.en: If you compensate for a lack of something or for something you have done wrong, you do something to show that you are sorry or that you are trying to make things better.

words.ex: His competence in math helped him solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面的能力帮助他解决了这个问题。
words.en: Competence is the ability to do something well or efficiently.

words.ex: He is a competent teacher who helps students easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有能力的老师，能轻松帮助学生。
words.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: He filed a complaint about the noisy neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他投诉了吵闹的邻居。
words.en: A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a particular situation.

words.ex: The completion of the project took three months.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的完成花了三个月。
words.en: The act of finishing or making something whole or perfect.

words.ex: Too many rules can complicate the game.
words.ex_cn: 太多的规则会使游戏变得复杂。
words.en: To make something more difficult to understand or deal with by adding more parts or details.

words.ex: The injury led to a complication in his recovery.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他的康复过程复杂化了。
words.en: A complication is a problem or difficulty that makes a situation harder to deal with.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.ex: A car has many components, like wheels and engines.
words.ex_cn: 汽车有许多部分，比如轮子和发动机。
words.en: A component is a part of a larger whole, especially a part that can be separated from or attached to a system.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.ex: The teacher explained the topic comprehensively.
words.ex_cn: 老师全面地讲解了这个主题。
words.en: In a way that includes or deals with all or nearly all elements or aspects of something.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.ex: He concluded that the experiment failed.
words.ex_cn: 他得出结论说实验失败了。
words.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.ex: Traffic congestion caused delays on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 交通堵塞导致了高速公路的延误。
words.en: Congestion refers to the state of being overcrowded, especially with traffic or people, or the condition of being blocked or clogged.

words.ex: The army conquered the small city after a long battle.
words.ex_cn: 军队经过长期战斗征服了这座小城。
words.en: To conquer means to take control of a country or city and its people by force, or to successfully deal with or control something.

words.ex: He is a conscientious student who always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个尽责的学生，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is conscientious is very careful to do their work properly.

words.ex: He was conscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后他醒了过来。
words.en: If you are conscious of something, you notice it or are aware of it.

words.ex: He asked for her consent before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始这个项目之前征求了她的同意。
words.en: Consent is permission for something to happen or agreement to do something.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: I consider going to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我考虑明天去公园。
words.en: If you consider something, you think about it carefully.

words.tr: adj. 考虑周到的；体贴的；
words.ex: He is considerate and always asks if others need help.
words.ex_cn: 他很体贴，总是问别人是否需要帮助。
words.en: Someone who is considerate pays attention to the needs, wishes, or feelings of other people.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.ex: He gave a constructive comment on my essay.
words.ex_cn: 他对我的论文给出了建设性的评论。
words.en: If something is constructive, it is useful and intended to help or improve something.

words.ex: He will consult a doctor for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他将咨询医生治疗他的头痛。
words.en: to seek information or advice from someone, especially someone who is an expert in a particular field

words.ex: The consumption of water has increased this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年水的消耗量增加了。
words.en: Consumption is the act of buying and using products.

words.ex: The contestant won the singing competition.
words.ex_cn: 这位竞争者赢得了歌唱比赛。
words.en: A contestant is someone who takes part in a competition or contest.

words.ex: The continual rain made the road very muddy.
words.ex_cn: 不停的雨让道路变得非常泥泞。
words.en: Something that is continual happens repeatedly over a period of time.

words.ex: He continually checks his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地查看手机。
words.en: If something happens continually, it happens without stopping or happening repeatedly over a period of time.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.ex: There was a controversy about the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 关于新校规，人们展开了争论。
words.en: A controversy is a disagreement or argument about something that involves many people and generates strong feelings.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的；有说服力的； v. 说服；“convince”的现在分词；
words.ex: His argument was convincing.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点令人信服。
words.en: A convincing argument, evidence, or person is one that makes you believe that something is true or right.

words.tr: n. 冷静；凉快；冷淡；厚颜无耻
words.ex: His coolness helped him stay calm during the test.
words.ex_cn: 他的冷静帮助他在考试期间保持镇定。
words.en: The quality or state of being cool; a moderate or refreshing degree of cold; lack of heat or warmth.

words.ex: The corporate office is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: Corporate relates to large companies or to a particular large company.

words.tr:
v. 使腐败；
adj. 腐败的；
words.ex: The official was corrupt by taking bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员因收受贿赂而腐败。
words.en: If someone is corrupt, they do things that are dishonest or illegal in order to gain money or power.

words.ex: The government punished the official for corruption.
words.ex_cn: 政府因贪污惩罚了那名官员。
words.en: Corruption is dishonest or illegal behavior, especially by people in positions of power.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.tr: adj. 无数的；多的；数不清的；
words.ex: There are countless stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数颗星星。
words.en: Too numerous to count.

words.ex: The courageous firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的消防员从着火的房子里救出了孩子。
words.en: Someone who is courageous shows courage.

words.tr: phrase. 覆盖范围的文字说明；用于描述某项服务或产品覆盖区域的标注文字
words.ex: The map includes a coverage lettering that explains the service areas.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图包含了一段文字说明，解释了服务范围。
words.en: Text or lettering used to describe or provide information about an insurance policy's coverage.

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.tr: n. 交会处；十字路口； v. 穿过；“cross”的现在分词；
words.ex: Be careful at the crossing near the school.
words.ex_cn: 在学校附近的交会处要小心。
words.en: A crossing is a place where something such as a road, river, or railway can be crossed safely.

words.ex: Farmers cultivate rice in the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植水稻。
words.en: To cultivate land means to prepare it and grow crops on it. To cultivate a particular quality, skill, or attitude means to try hard to develop it and make it stronger.

words.ex: The farmer's cultivation of rice takes months.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植水稻需要几个月的时间。
words.en: The process of trying to acquire or develop a quality or skill.

words.ex: It is customary to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是习惯做法。
words.en: Something that is customary is normal because it is the way something is usually done.

words.ex: The company made a cutback on office supplies.
words.ex_cn: 公司减少了办公用品的开支。
words.en: A reduction in something, especially in the amount of money spent on a particular thing.

words.ex: This phone has cutting-edge technology.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机拥有尖端技术。
words.en: Something that is cutting-edge is at the forefront of technological or other developments.

words.tr: adj. 日常的；每日的；过一天算一天的
words.ex: He handles day-to-day tasks at work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中处理日常事务。
words.en: relating to or occurring in the course of ordinary days; routine.

words.ex: She works at a day-care center.
words.ex_cn: 她在一家日间托儿中心工作。
words.en: Day-care refers to the care of children during the day by people who are not their parents, especially while the parents are at work.

words.ex: He had a daydream about winning the lottery.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个中彩票的白日梦。
words.en: A daydream is a series of pleasant thoughts about something you would like to happen, often about something that is unlikely to happen.

words.tr:
n. 首次露面；初次登场
v. 初次登场；首次推出
words.ex: He made his debut on stage last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚在舞台上首次登台。
words.en: The debut of a performer or sports player is their first public performance, appearance, or recording.

words.ex: The country made a declaration of independence.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家发表了独立宣言。
words.en: A declaration is a formal statement or announcement.

words.tr: adj. 专注的；专用的；献身的； v. 奉献；“dedicate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is dedicated to his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他专注于学习。
words.en: If you say that someone is dedicated to something, you approve of the fact that they have committed to it and are willing to give a lot of time and energy to it.

words.ex: His dedication to teaching helped many students succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他对教学的奉献帮助了许多学生取得成功。
words.en: The act of dedicating or the state of being dedicated; commitment.

words.ex: His deduction was based on the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的推论基于证据。
words.en: A deduction is a conclusion that you reach about something because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: The rain deepened the puddles on the road.
words.ex_cn: 雨水加深了路上的水坑。
words.en: If a situation or emotion deepens or if something deepens it, it becomes stronger and more intense.

words.ex: The defect in the phone made it hard to use.
words.ex_cn: 手机的缺陷让它很难使用。
words.en: A defect is a fault or imperfection in a person or thing.

words.ex: His deficiency in math made him struggle in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的缺乏让他在课堂上很吃力。
words.en: A deficiency is a lack or shortage of something that is needed.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.ex: The manager will delegate the task to her assistant.
words.ex_cn: 经理将把这个任务委派给她的助手。
words.en: A delegate is a person who is chosen or elected to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of people, especially at a conference or a meeting. As a verb, to delegate means to give a task or responsibility to another person, especially someone who is less senior than you.

words.tr: v. 兑现；递送；交付；发表；为…接生；
words.ex: He promised to deliver on his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺要兑现自己的目标。
words.en: To bring and hand over (a letter, parcel, or ordered goods) to the proper recipient or address.

words.ex: The density of water is 1 gram per cubic centimeter.
words.ex_cn: 水的密度是每立方厘米1克。
words.en: Density is a measure of how much mass is contained in a given unit volume of a substance.

words.ex: He uses deodorant every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都用除臭剂。
words.en: A deodorant is a substance that you can use on your body to prevent or mask the smell of sweat.

words.ex: You need to pay a 40-yuan deposit to rent the bike.
words.ex_cn: 租自行车需要支付40元押金。
words.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it. It is also a sum of money that you pay into a bank account.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏足够教育的；贫穷的； v. 剥夺；使丧失；“deprive”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: Children from deprived areas often struggle to read and write.
words.ex_cn: 来自教育缺乏地区的儿童常常难以阅读和写作。
words.en: If you are deprived of something that you want or need, you do not have it.

words.ex: The deputy signed the document for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 代理人替经理签署了文件。
words.en: A deputy is a person who is appointed to act as a substitute for another, especially in a position of authority.

words.tr: adj. 废弃的；荒芜的；被遗弃的； v. “desert”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The deserted house had broken windows and overgrown grass.
words.ex_cn: 那座废弃的房子有破碎的窗户和茂盛的杂草。
words.en: If a place is deserted, there are no people in it.

words.tr:
n. 设计；图案；花样；企图；图谋；
v. 设计；计划；谋划；构思；
words.ex: The dress has a beautiful design.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子有一个美丽的设计。
words.en: To design something means to plan and make a detailed drawing of it, or to plan and create something in a skillful or artistic way.

words.ex: He believed his destiny was to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己的命运是成为一名医生。
words.en: Destiny is the force which some people believe controls the things that happen to you in your life.

words.tr: adj. 分离的； v. 脱离；拆卸；分离；“detach”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is detached from the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子与邻居的房子是分开的。
words.en: If someone is detached, they do not have any emotional interest in a situation and therefore can make fair decisions.

words.ex: I can detect a change in her mood.
words.ex_cn: 我能察觉到她情绪的变化。
words.en: To detect something means to find it or discover it, often using special equipment or methods.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: The teacher will determine the winner of the contest.
words.ex_cn: 老师将确定比赛的获胜者。
words.en: If you determine something, you decide it or settle it.

words.tr: v. 毁灭；摧毁；“devastate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 非常伤心的；
words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: If you are devastated by something, you are very shocked and upset by it. If a place is devastated, it is severely damaged or destroyed.

words.tr: adj. 毁灭性的； v. “devastate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The earthquake caused devastating damage to the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震对这座城市造成了毁灭性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as devastating, you are emphasizing that it is very harmful or damaging.

words.ex: The developer built a new apartment complex.
words.ex_cn: 这家开发商建造了一座新的公寓楼。
words.en: A developer is a person or a company that develops software, websites, or applications, or that builds houses or other structures on land.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.ex: The truck runs on diesel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车使用柴油运行。
words.en: Diesel is a type of heavy oil used as fuel in diesel engines.

words.ex: Can you differentiate between the two colors?
words.ex_cn: 你能区分这两种颜色吗？
words.en: To differentiate means to recognize or express the difference between things or people.

words.ex: The stomach digests food into nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 胃将食物消化成营养物质。
words.en: To digest means to break down food in the stomach and intestines into substances that can be absorbed by the body. It can also mean to understand or assimilate information. As a noun, it refers to a compilation or summary of information.

words.ex: Good digestion helps your body absorb nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 良好的消化有助于身体吸收营养。
words.en: The process by which food is broken down in the stomach and intestines so that the body can absorb it and use it for energy and nutrients.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: He is a diplomatic ambassador who handles international relations.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位处理国际关系的外交大使。
words.en: Diplomatic means relating to diplomacy or diplomats, or using skill and tact in dealing with people.

words.ex: He asked for the direction to the station.
words.ex_cn: 他问了去车站的方向。
words.en: A direction is the way that you have to travel to get from one place to another, or the way that something is moving or pointing.

words.ex: I looked up his phone number in the directory.
words.ex_cn: 我在姓名地址录里查了他的电话号码。
words.en: A directory is a book or list which gives names, addresses, and other information about people or organizations.

words.tr: adj. 处于不利地位的；贫困的； v. “disadvantage”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The school helps disadvantaged children with free meals.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校为处境不利的孩子提供免费餐食。
words.en: People who are disadvantaged do not have the same opportunities or advantages as other people, often because of their financial situation or social position.

words.ex: He showed his disapproval by staying silent.
words.ex_cn: 他通过保持沉默表示反对。
words.en: Disapproval is the feeling that someone or something is bad, wrong, or unacceptable.

words.ex: The storm caused disastrous damage to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给村庄造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as disastrous, you mean that it is very unfortunate or unsuccessful.

words.ex: The hard chair caused him discomfort.
words.ex_cn: 这把硬椅子让他感到不舒适。
words.en: Discomfort is a feeling of slight pain or physical unease, or a feeling of worry or embarrassment.

words.ex: He felt discontent with his job.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的工作感到不满。
words.en: Discontent is a feeling of being unhappy because you are not satisfied with your situation or with what you have.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: He noticed the discrimination between the two prices.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了两个价格之间的区别。
words.en: The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.

words.tr:
adj. 厌恶的；憎恶的；反感的
v. 使厌恶；使作呕；“disgust”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt disgusted when he saw the dirty kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到脏乱的厨房时，他感到厌恶。
words.en: If you are disgusted, you feel a strong sense of dislike and disapproval towards something unpleasant or offensive.

words.tr: adv. 不诚实地；不正直地
words.ex: He obtained the money dishonestly.
words.ex_cn: 他不诚实地获得了这笔钱。
words.en: In a manner that is not honest; deceitfully.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: His dismissal made him very sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的被解雇让他非常难过。
words.en: The act of officially removing someone from their job, or the act of sending someone away or allowing them to leave.

words.ex: The room was in complete disorder.
words.ex_cn: 房间一片混乱。
words.en: A disorder is a state of confusion or untidiness, or a medical problem that affects the mind or body.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: The displacement of the car was 10 meters east.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的位移是向东10米。
words.en: The act of moving something from its place or position, or the condition of having been moved from it.

words.tr:
n. 不尊敬；无礼；轻蔑
v. 不尊重
words.ex: He showed disrespect to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师表现出不尊重。
words.en: If someone shows disrespect, they speak or behave in a way that shows lack of respect for someone or something.

words.ex: The storm caused a disruption in the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴扰乱了火车服务。
words.en: Disruption is a situation in which something is prevented from continuing in its usual way because of problems or difficulties.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

words.ex: Sugar dissolves in water.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中溶解。
words.en: If a substance dissolves in liquid or if you dissolve a substance, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.

words.ex: The two colors are distinct.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色有区别。
words.en: If something is distinct, it is easily seen, heard, or understood.

words.ex: This painting has a distinctive style.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有独特的风格。
words.en: Something that is distinctive has a special quality or feature which makes it easily recognizable and different from other things of the same type.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.ex: The loud music was a distraction while I tried to study.
words.ex_cn: 当我试图学习时，大声的音乐让我分心。
words.en: Something that makes it difficult for you to concentrate on what you are doing.

words.ex: He felt great distress when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到非常忧虑。
words.en: Distress is a feeling of extreme worry, sadness, or pain.

words.tr: adj. 烦恼的； v. “distress”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She looked distressed after hearing the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 听到坏消息后，她显得很烦恼。
words.en: If someone is distressed, they are extremely upset.

words.ex: The distribution of students in the class is even.
words.ex_cn: 班级里学生的分布是均匀的。
words.en: The process of giving out or spreading something, or the way in which something is spread or arranged over an area or among a group of people.

words.ex: The noise from the construction caused a disturbance.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的噪音造成了干扰。
words.en: A disturbance is an event or situation in which people behave in a noisy or violent way, or something that interrupts what you are doing.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.ex: The ship arrived at the dock at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 船在日出时到达了码头。
words.en: A dock is an enclosed area of water in a port where ships go to be loaded, unloaded, and repaired.

words.ex: He is an expert in the domain of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 他是人工智能领域的专家。
words.en: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.

words.ex: The dominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间占优势的颜色是蓝色。
words.en: Someone or something that is dominant is more powerful, successful, influential, or noticeable than other people or things.

words.ex: The empire's domination over the region lasted for centuries.
words.ex_cn: 这个帝国对该地区的统治持续了几个世纪。
words.en: The exercise of control or influence over someone or something, or the state of being so controlled.

words.tr: adj. 实际的；脚踏实地的
words.ex: He is a down-to-earth man who helps everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个脚踏实地的人，乐于帮助每个人。
words.en: If you say that someone is down-to-earth, you approve of the fact that they concern themselves with practical things and actions, rather than with abstract theories.

words.ex: The downside of this job is the long hours.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作的负面是工作时间很长。
words.en: The downside of something is the aspect of it which is less positive, pleasant, or useful than its other aspects.

words.tr:
adv. 向下地；
adj. 向下的；
words.ex: The leaves fell downward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 树叶慢慢向下飘落。
words.en: Moving or leading towards a lower place or level

words.ex: The leaves fell downwards.
words.ex_cn: 树叶往下落。
words.en: Moving or leading towards a lower place or level.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.ex: The new policy drastically reduced costs.
words.ex_cn: 新政策大幅度降低了成本。
words.en: In a way that is likely to have a strong or far-reaching effect.

words.ex: He wrote a draft of the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送之前写了这封信的草稿。
words.en: A draft is a preliminary version of a piece of writing, or a current of air in a room or other confined space. It can also refer to the act of selecting someone for a particular purpose or task, especially in sports or the military.

words.ex: The drawback of this phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的缺点是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A drawback is a feature of something that makes it less useful or desirable than it could be.

words.ex: He has a dual role as teacher and coach.
words.ex_cn: 他同时担任老师和教练的双重角色。
words.en: Having two parts or aspects.

words.tr: adj. 阴暗的；枯燥的；无趣的；
words.ex: The room was dull because the windows were covered.
words.ex_cn: 房间很阴暗，因为窗户被遮住了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as dull, you mean they are not interesting or exciting.

words.ex: He gave a dumb answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个愚笨的回答。
words.en: If someone is dumb, they are unable to speak. If you describe someone or something as dumb, you mean that they are stupid or silly.

words.ex: He dumped the trash into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把垃圾倒进了垃圾桶。
words.en: To dump something means to get rid of it quickly and without care, often because it is no longer wanted or needed. It can also refer to the place where waste is left.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.ex: He studies ecology to understand how animals live with plants.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生态学以了解动物如何与植物共存。
words.en: Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment; it seeks to understand the vital connections between plants and animals and the world around them.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.ex: The effectiveness of the new medicine was proven in trials.
words.ex_cn: 这种新药的有效性在试验中得到了证实。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.ex: He fixed the electrical wire with tape.
words.ex_cn: 他用胶带修好了电线。
words.en: Relating to electricity or things that use electricity.

words.ex: Her dress showed great elegance.
words.ex_cn: 她的裙子展现了极大的优雅。
words.en: Elegance is the quality of being graceful and stylish in appearance or manner.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的；合意的；
words.ex: He is eligible to vote because he is 18 years old.
words.ex_cn: 他年满18岁，有资格投票。
words.en: Someone who is eligible for something is qualified or allowed to do it.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: The factory reduces emission to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 工厂减少排放以保护环境。
words.en: An emission is the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.

words.ex: The emperor ruled the country for many years.
words.ex_cn: 这位皇帝统治这个国家很多年。
words.en: A male sovereign ruler of an empire.

words.ex: The empire ruled many countries long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这个帝国很久以前统治了许多国家。
words.en: An empire is a group of countries or territories that are under the control of a single ruler or government.

words.ex: The company will employ five new workers next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司下个月将雇佣五名新员工。
words.en: If a person or company employs you, they pay you to work for them.

words.ex: The police enforce the law.
words.ex_cn: 警察强制执行法律。
words.en: If people in authority enforce a law or a rule, they make sure that it is obeyed, usually by punishing people who do not obey it.

words.tr: v. 参与；从事；吸引；与…建立密切关系；
words.ex: He engages in community volunteer work.
words.ex_cn: 他参与社区志愿工作。
words.en: To engage means to occupy, attract, or involve someone or oneself in a particular activity or situation.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.ex: The new job enriched his life.
words.ex_cn: 这份新工作使他的生活富裕起来。
words.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, often by adding something to it.

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.ex: The environmentalist plants trees every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 这位环保主义者每周末都植树。
words.en: An environmentalist is a person who is concerned with protecting the environment.

words.ex: I envisage a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 我设想一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: If you envisage something, you imagine that it is true, real, or likely to happen.

words.ex: He envisions a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 他想象一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: To envision something is to imagine it as a future possibility; it is often used to describe the act of foreseeing or planning for the future.

words.ex: The equation is easy to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这个方程式很容易解。
words.en: An equation is a mathematical statement that asserts the equality of two expressions.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.ex: Water causes erosion of the soil.
words.ex_cn: 水会导致土壤腐蚀。
words.en: The process by which the surface of the earth is worn away by the action of water, glaciers, winds, waves, etc.

words.ex: The establishment of the school took five years.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的建立花了五年时间。
words.en: The act of establishing something or the state of being established. It can also refer to an organization or institution, especially a business or public body.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.ex: The teacher gave an evaluation of the student's work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作业进行了评估。
words.en: An evaluation is a judgment about how good, useful, or successful something is.

words.ex: The bird evolved from a small dinosaur.
words.ex_cn: 这种鸟由一种小型恐龙演变而来。
words.en: If something evolves or you evolve it, it gradually develops over a period of time into something different and usually more advanced.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.ex: His story was an exaggeration of the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事是对事实的夸张。
words.en: An exaggeration is a statement that represents something as better or worse than it really is.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.ex: He is exceptionally good at math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面异常出色。
words.en: To an unusual degree; extremely.

words.tr:
n. 过量；过度；超过；
adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The excess of sugar in his diet caused health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食中糖分过量导致了健康问题。
words.en: An excess of something is a larger amount than is needed, allowed, or usual.

words.ex: He ate excessive amounts of candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了过多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.

words.ex: The rule excludes children under 12.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则排除了12岁以下的孩子。
words.en: To exclude someone or something means to prevent them from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.ex: He uses this park exclusively for walking.
words.ex_cn: 他只在这个公园散步。
words.en: If you do something exclusively, you do it only in the way mentioned, and not in any other way.

words.tr:
n. 决策人；行政官；管理人员；
adj. 行政的；决策的；
words.ex: The executive decided to launch the new product.
words.ex_cn: 这位决策人决定推出新产品。
words.en: An executive is a person who has a senior management position in a business or other organization.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.ex: The report gives an exhaustive list of all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告给出了所有规则的详尽列表。
words.en: If you describe a study, search, or list as exhaustive, you mean that it is very thorough and complete.

words.ex: The museum will exhibit ancient coins next month.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆下个月将展览古钱币。
words.en: To exhibit something means to show it in a public place so that people can go to see it. It can also mean to show a particular quality, ability, or type of behavior.

words.ex: Dinosaurs existed millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙存在于数百万年前。
words.en: If something exists, it is present in the world as a real thing.

words.ex: His monthly expenses are too high.
words.ex_cn: 他的月支出太高了。
words.en: Expenses are the costs incurred in the process of doing something or the money spent on something.

words.ex: The exploration of space takes many years.
words.ex_cn: 太空探索需要很多年。
words.en: The act of searching for the purpose of discovery of information or resources.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: The exterior of the house is painted white.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观是白色的。
words.en: The outer surface or structure of something.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The extinction of dinosaurs happened millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的灭绝发生在数百万年前。
words.en: The state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct.

words.tr:
n. 性格外向者；爱交际的人
adj. 外向的
words.ex: He is an extrovert who loves talking to people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的人，喜欢和人交谈。
words.en: An extrovert is someone who is very outgoing, sociable, and enjoys being around other people.

words.tr: n. 织物；（建筑物的）结构；
words.ex: The dress is made of soft fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子是由柔软的织物制成的。
words.en: Fabric refers to cloth or other material produced by weaving together cotton, nylon, wool, silk, or other threads. It can also refer to the basic structure of a building or a system.

words.ex: The concert was fabulous!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something as fabulous, you are emphasizing that you like it a lot or think that it is very good.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.ex: The teacher showed fairness in grading all students.
words.ex_cn: 老师在给所有学生评分时展现了公平。
words.en: Fairness is the quality of treating people equally or in a way that is right or reasonable.

words.tr:
v. 伪造；假装；冒充；
adj. 假的；冒充的；伪造的；
words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.ex: The magic show had a strange fascination for children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演对孩子们有一种奇特的迷惑力。
words.en: A fascination is a very strong interest or attraction for someone or something.

words.ex: The fatty meat made him feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 这块脂肪太多的肉让他感到恶心。
words.en: containing a lot of fat; oily or greasy

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.ex: They had a feast on New Year's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他们在元旦举办了一场盛宴。
words.en: A feast is a large and special meal, often to celebrate something.

words.tr:
v. 喂；吃；
n. 饲养；喂养；
words.ex: She feeds the cat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上喂猫。
words.en: To give food to a person or an animal; to supply something to a machine or a system.

words.ex: She has a feminine voice.
words.ex_cn: 她的声音很女性化。
words.en: having qualities or an appearance traditionally associated with women, especially delicacy and prettiness.

words.ex: He eats fibre to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃纤维来保持健康。
words.en: Fibre refers to a thread or filament from which a vegetable tissue, mineral substance, or textile is formed. It can also denote dietary material containing substances such as cellulose, lignin, and pectin, which are resistant to the action of digestive enzymes.

words.ex: He loves reading science fiction.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读科幻小说。
words.en: Fiction refers to literature in the form of prose, especially novels, that describes imaginary events and people.

words.ex: The floor was filthy after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨过后，地板变得非常肮脏。
words.en: Something that is filthy is extremely dirty.

words.ex: She has a flair for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她有绘画的天赋。
words.en: If you have a flair for a particular activity, you have a natural ability to do it well.

words.ex: The flaw in the glass made it break easily.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃上的瑕疵让它很容易碎。
words.en: A flaw is a mistake or weakness in something that makes it less effective or valuable.

words.ex: He will flee from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 他会从着火的房子里逃走。
words.en: If you flee from something or someone, you leave them quickly because you are afraid of them or because you do not want to be involved with them.

words.ex: The navy launched a large fleet to protect the coast.
words.ex_cn: 海军派出了一支大型舰队来保护海岸。
words.en: A fleet is a group of ships or vehicles that are controlled by one company or organization and are used for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
n. 流动；
v. 流动；
words.ex: The flow of water in the river is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 河里水的流动非常快。
words.en: To move along or out steadily and continuously in a current or stream.

words.ex: He heard a footstep behind him.
words.ex_cn: 他听到身后有脚步声。
words.en: A footstep is the sound or mark that is made by someone walking each time their foot touches the ground.

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.ex: He formally accepted the award at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上正式接受了奖项。
words.en: in a formal manner

words.tr:
n. 格式；
v. 格式化；
words.ex: The file is in PDF format.
words.ex_cn: 这个文件是PDF格式。
words.en: The way in which something is arranged or set out.

words.ex: The company used a new formula to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 公司使用了一个新方案来解决问题。
words.en: A formula is a plan or method that is used to achieve a particular goal, especially in science or mathematics.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.ex: The foundation gives money to poor students.
words.ex_cn: 这个基金会向贫困学生提供资金。
words.en: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

words.ex: There is friction between the two neighbors over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居因为篱笆问题产生了不和。
words.en: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

words.ex: The loud noise gave her a sudden fright.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让她吓了一跳。
words.en: A sudden intense feeling of fear.

words.ex: The meeting was fruitful and solved many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议富有成效，解决了许多问题。
words.en: Producing good or helpful results; productive.

words.tr: adj. 失意的；挫败的； v. “frustrate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt frustrated when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 当他考试不及格时，他感到失意。
words.en: If you are frustrated, you are upset or angry because you are unable to do anything about a situation.

words.tr: adj. 令人沮丧的；令人泄气的；让人懊恼的； v. “frustrate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The slow internet is frustrating.
words.ex_cn: 网速慢让人沮丧。
words.en: If something is frustrating, it annoys you or makes you angry because you cannot do anything about the problems it causes.

words.tr: n. 烟雾；烟气；“fume”的复数； v. 大为生气；
words.ex: The car released black fumes from its exhaust.
words.ex_cn: 汽车从排气管冒出黑烟。
words.en: Fumes are the strong, often unpleasant smell or smoke that is given off by a substance.

words.tr:
n. 基金；资金；
v. 提供资金；
words.ex: The school raised a fund for new books.
words.ex_cn: 学校为购买新书筹集了一笔基金。
words.en: A sum of money saved or made available for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 资金；款项；拨款； v. “fund”的现在分词；
words.ex: The school needs more funding for new books.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校需要更多资金来购买新书。
words.en: Funding is money which is used to pay for a particular activity or to help achieve a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 布置家具；“furnish”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 配备家具的；
words.ex: They furnished the apartment with new tables and chairs.
words.ex_cn: 他们给公寓布置了新的桌椅。
words.en: If a room or building is furnished, it is equipped with furniture.

words.ex: There's no need to make a fuss about a small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 一个小错误没必要大惊小怪。
words.en: If you make a fuss or kick up a fuss about something, you become angry or excited about it and complain.

words.ex: He bought a new gadget to clean his kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个新的小器具来清洁厨房。
words.en: A gadget is a small device or machine with a particular purpose.

words.tr:
v. 获得；增加；
n. 增益；获得；
words.ex: He gained a new skill last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月获得了一项新技能。
words.en: To gain means to obtain something that is useful, that gives you an advantage, or that is in some way positive, especially over a period of time.

words.ex: She bought a new garment for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件新衣服。
words.en: A garment is a piece of clothing; used especially in contexts where you are talking about the manufacture or sale of clothes.

words.tr: n. 收集；采集；聚会；聚集； v. 聚集；集合；“gather”的现在分词；
words.ex: The gathering of old books took him years.
words.ex_cn: 收集旧书花了他多年时间。
words.en: A gathering is a group of people meeting together for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He has a gene that makes him tall.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个让他长高的基因。
words.en: A gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity. Genes, which are made up of DNA, act as instructions to make molecules called proteins.

words.ex: He made a generalization from the data.
words.ex_cn: 他从数据中做出了一个概括。
words.en: A generalization is a statement that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: He generalized the results from the small group to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他将小群体的结果概括为全体情况。
words.en: If you generalize, you say something that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: He gave a generous donation to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地捐钱给穷人。
words.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

words.ex: The scientist studied genetic traits in plants.
words.ex_cn: 科学家研究了植物的基因特征。
words.en: relating to genes or heredity

words.ex: He is a genius in math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面是个天才。
words.en: Someone who is a genius is a person who is exceptionally intelligent or talented, especially in a particular field.

words.tr: adj. 温和的；文雅的；温柔的；
words.ex: The mother gave a gentle hug to her child.
words.ex_cn: 母亲给了孩子一个温和的拥抱。
words.en: Someone who is gentle is kind and calm, and does not behave in a violent or harsh way.

words.tr: phrase. 经过基因改造的；转基因的
words.ex: The corn is genetically modified to resist pests.
words.ex_cn: 这种玉米经过基因改造以抵抗害虫。
words.en: Genetically modified refers to an organism whose genetic material has been altered using genetic engineering techniques.

words.ex: He loves studying geology in high school.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在高中学习地质学。
words.en: The science which deals with the physical structure and substance of the earth, their history, and the processes which act on them.

words.ex: Washing hands can kill germs.
words.ex_cn: 洗手可以杀死病菌。
words.en: A germ is a very small organism that causes disease.

words.ex: She likes swimming, which is a gerund.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢游泳，这是一个动名词。
words.en: A gerund is a noun formed from a verb which refers to an action, process, or state. In English, gerunds end in -ing (e.g., 'swimming' in 'Swimming is good exercise.').

words.ex: He made a gesture of welcome with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用手做了一个欢迎的姿态。
words.en: A gesture is a movement that you make with a part of your body, especially your hands, to express emotion or information.

words.tr:
adj. 巨大的；伟大的；
n. 巨人；伟人；
words.ex: The giant elephant stood near the tree.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的大象站在树旁。
words.en: A giant is an imaginary person who is very big and strong, especially one mentioned in old stories. In everyday language, a giant can also refer to a very large and successful company or organization.

words.tr: adj. 有才华的；有天赋的；
words.ex: He is a gifted musician who plays piano beautifully.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有才华的音乐家，钢琴弹得非常优美。
words.en: Having a natural ability or talent.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.ex: I caught a glimpse of the cat before it ran away.
words.ex_cn: 我在它跑掉之前瞥了一眼那只猫。
words.en: A glimpse is a brief, quick look at something or someone.

words.ex: Globalization helps countries trade more easily.
words.ex_cn: 全球化帮助各国更容易地进行贸易。
words.en: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.

words.ex: The sun shone with great glory at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时分，太阳闪耀着辉煌的光辉。
words.en: High renown or honor won by notable achievements; magnificence or great beauty.

words.ex: She walked with grace across the stage.
words.ex_cn: 她优雅地走过舞台。
words.en: Grace is the quality of being pleasant, polite, and dignified, or a period of time allowed for something to be done.

words.tr: adj. 优雅的；优美的；得体的；
words.ex: The dancer moved in a graceful way.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者动作优雅。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as graceful, you mean that they move in a smooth, controlled, and attractive way.

words.ex: The hotel has a five-star grade.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店有五星级别的等级。
words.en: A grade is a level of quality, rank, or value, or a mark given in an examination or for school work.

words.tr:
adj. 壮丽的；堂皇的；重大的；总的；
n. 大钢琴；
words.ex: The grand castle stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 壮丽的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: If you describe a building or a piece of scenery as grand, you mean that its size or appearance is very impressive.

words.tr:
v. 领会；抓紧；
n. 领会；
words.ex: I couldn't grasp the meaning of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 我没能领会这首诗的含义。
words.en: To grasp something means to take it in your hand and hold it firmly.

words.ex: His greed made him steal money from his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪让他偷了朋友的钱。
words.en: Greed is the desire to have more of something, such as food or money, than is necessary or fair.

words.tr:
n. 烤架；铁格子
v. 烧烤；拷问
words.ex: He cooked the burgers on the grill.
words.ex_cn: 他用烤架烤了汉堡。
words.en: To cook food on a metal frame over a fire, or a metal frame used for cooking food in this way.

words.tr: adj. 扣人心弦的； v. “grip”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie had a gripping plot that kept me awake all night.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影情节扣人心弦，让我整晚都没睡。
words.en: If something is gripping, it holds your interest or attention because it is exciting or intense.

words.ex: The gross income of the company is $5 million.
words.ex_cn: 公司的总收入是500万美元。
words.en: If you describe something as gross, you mean it is very obvious, unacceptable, or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 性情乖戾的；脾气暴躁的
words.ex: He is grumpy when he wakes up early.
words.ex_cn: 他早起时会脾气不好。
words.en: If you say that someone is grumpy, you mean that they are bad-tempered and miserable.

words.ex: Follow the guideline to complete the form.
words.ex_cn: 按照指导路线完成表格。
words.en: A guideline is a set of rules or instructions that are given by an official organization telling you how to do something, especially something difficult.

words.tr: n. 栖息地；居留地；产地；
words.ex: The panda's habitat is in the mountains of China.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫的栖息地在中国的山区。
words.en: The natural environment in which a species or group of species lives.

words.ex: He reported the harassment to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他向警察报告了骚扰行为。
words.en: Harassment is behaviour which is intended to trouble or annoy someone, especially repeated behaviour.

words.ex: He faced many hardships during the war.
words.ex_cn: 他在战争期间经历了许多困苦。
words.en: Hardship refers to a situation that is difficult to endure because of lack of money, resources, or other basic necessities.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.ex: He felt hatred for the man who hurt his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他憎恨那个伤害他兄弟的人。
words.en: Hatred is an extremely strong feeling of dislike for someone or something.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.tr: v. 朝向；前进；“head”的现在分词； n. 标题；
words.ex: The ship is heading north.
words.ex_cn: 船正朝北航行。
words.en: A heading is a word, phrase, or sentence at the beginning of a written passage that explains what it's about.

words.tr: phrase. 卫生保健；健康护理
words.ex: He works in health care as a nurse.
words.ex_cn: 他作为一名护士从事医疗工作。
words.en: Health care refers to the organized provision of medical care to individuals or a community.

words.ex: The sky looks heavenly at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时天空看起来像天上的。
words.en: If you describe something as heavenly, you mean that it is extremely pleasant or enjoyable.

words.ex: Her mornings are hectic with work and kids.
words.ex_cn: 她的早晨因为工作和孩子而紧张忙碌。
words.en: If you describe a situation as hectic, you mean that it is very busy and involves a lot of rushed activity.

words.ex: The child felt helpless when he lost his mother.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子失去妈妈时，他感到无助。
words.en: Unable to defend oneself or to act without help.

words.ex: It rained all day, hence the game was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 下了一整天的雨，因此比赛被取消了。
words.en: You use hence to indicate that the statement you are about to make is a consequence of what you have just said.

words.ex: The heroic firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这位英勇的消防员从着火的房子里救出了孩子。
words.en: If you describe a person or their actions as heroic, you admire them because they show extreme bravery.

words.ex: The movie was hilarious and made us laugh a lot.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常搞笑，让我们笑得很开心。
words.en: If you describe something as hilarious, you mean that it is extremely funny and it makes you laugh a lot.

words.ex: The historian wrote a book about ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 这位历史学家写了一本关于古罗马的书。
words.en: A historian is a person who studies or writes about history; an expert in history.

words.ex: Historically, people used abacus for counting.
words.ex_cn: 历史上，人们用算盘进行计算。
words.en: In a way that relates to the study of past events.

words.ex: The church is a holy place.
words.ex_cn: 教堂是一个神圣的地方。
words.en: If you describe something as holy, you mean that it is considered to be special because it is connected with God or a particular religion.

words.ex: The homeless man slept on the bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个无家可归的人睡在长椅上。
words.en: If someone is homeless, they have no permanent place to live.

words.ex: I feel honoured to be invited to speak at the conference.
words.ex_cn: 我感到很荣幸被邀请在会议上发言。
words.en: Feeling proud and happy because you have been given special respect or a special opportunity.

words.ex: The frog hopped over the stone.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙跃过了那块石头。
words.en: To move by jumping on one foot or to move quickly and lightly from one place to another.

words.ex: The line is horizontal on the graph.
words.ex_cn: 这条线在图上是水平的。
words.en: Parallel to the plane of the horizon; at right angles to the vertical.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
